text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing recurring 99th tail on eu-west dedicated low-latency pool since ~09:10 UTC. P50 fine, but p99 jumps ~80-120ms for short chat requests.

ajay: saw that too. NV stats show GPU utilization steady, but packets retransmit count up on node NICs.

sasha: any kernel qdisc / eBPF shaping recently rolled?

maria: ops team pushed a network policing change yesterday evening to handle a noisy tenant, might be related.

ajay: quick probe: on node-12 I ran `ss -s` and `tc -s qdisc show dev eth0` — lots of drops on fq_codel ingress.

maria: paste of tcp summary: 
```
09:18:12 IP node-12 -> proxy: retransmits=214 rtt=2ms rttvar=1ms
09:18:13 drops=102 out of 10k pkts
```

lee: that matches a pattern where netpol shunts heavy flows to a policing path that adds microbursts -> kernel force-queue -> userspace TCP stalls -> GPU kernels block waiting on IO.

katie: low-latency tier is sensitive to even tiny jitter. We saw KV cache miss spike at the same time, so small packet loss cascaded to longer request times.

ops-oncall: ops confirmed the network appliance is doing per-tenant policing with a 10ms burst window for the suspect tenant. Policy id: netpol-2026-04.

maria: thinking mitigation options: 1) temporary carveout of critical traffic to a dedicated egress NIC on host, 2) bump fq_codel limits, or 3) route low-latency tenant to separate dedicated pool (cost).

ajay: quick test we can try: enable RX polling (ethtool -C eth0 rx-usecs 0) and 1) increase ingress qdisc target to 8ms. Not ideal but low risk for short canary.

sasha: +1 for a short canary on a single rack. We should synthetic-run chat 1k qps for 10m and compare p99.

lee: alternative software fix: add tenant token to proxy and mark requests as low-latency, then the router can preferentially route to low-jitter hosts. That needs a small proxy change.

katie: cost sense — if we create a tiny dedicated pool (4 GPUs) pinned to low-latency customers, estimate extra monthly cost ~ $12k for eu-west. But gives clean SLA.

maria: for immediate: will open a short-lived kernel tweak canary on rack eu-west-4. Plan: (A) enable rx-usecs=0 on two hosts, (B) set `tc qdisc change dev eth0 root fq_codel target 8ms limit 1000`, (C) run synthetic and monitor p99 and retransmits.

ajay: commands i ran (copyable):
```bash
ethtool -C eth0 rx-usecs 0 rx-frames 0
tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root fq_codel target 8ms limit 1000
# run synthetic probe
curl -X POST https://synthetic.local/run -d '{"qps":1000, "dur":600}'
```

ops-oncall: deploying the kernel tweak to canary hosts now. tagging with `canary/netpol-eu4` in deploy system.

deploy-bot: deploy started for canary/netpol-eu4 on hosts [node-12,node-13] by ops-oncall

lee: add a shortstats dashboard panel: p99 latency, NIC retransmits, fq_codel drops, kvcache hitrate.

katie: i'll model cost/benefit if canary shows persistent tail after netpol revert. If persistent, we propose 4-GPU carveout for lowlat.

sasha: if canary fails to improve, next step is to ask network to relax the 10ms burst policy for tenants that register as low-latency — needs ACL + tagging work.

maria: action items:
- ops-oncall: run canary and post results (owner: ops-oncall)
- ajay: prepare eBPF probe to measure per-process packet stalls (owner: ajay)
- lee: add dashboard panels (owner: lee)
- katie: cost estimate for 4-GPU carveout (owner: katie)

ajay: will also capture `bpftrace -e 'kprobe:tcp_sendmsg { @[comm] = count(); }'` for quick correlation.

ops-oncall: canary completed — preliminary: p99 improved from ~110ms -> ~30ms on the two hosts, retransmits down 70%. Full results in 15m.

maria: nice. if numbers hold, we should roll tweak to other racks and coordinate with network to remove the tenant-level policing until we finish router tagging.

katie: i'll sketch the pricing proposal and a targeted SL uplift for lowlat customers to offset the carveout.

lee: filing a runbook note: when netpol is enabled, expect microburst policing to cause tail for <50ms workloads — include quick tests.

maria: thanks all. keep thread updated. I posted data to the incident board: https://redwood.internal/ops/incident/5598765432

sasha: fyi tagging the tenant as `noisy-2026` so the net team can audit traffic.

ops-oncall: final results: 30m after canary, p99 stable ~28-35ms on canary hosts, others still at 90-120ms. Will schedule broader rollout + network coordination tomorrow. :thumbsup:

maria: great, closing loop here.
